rationale: Build on the current best late-aligned decoder-skip recurrent-tail baseline, but give each repeated tail block a tiny zero-init two-scalar control over recurrent attention vs recurrent MLP strength. This is a new recurrence-scheduling idea rather than another LR or head sweep, keeps shapes/step structure compile-stable, adds negligible size, preserves the winning late skip alignment, and directly targets the recurrent tail that has carried the strongest local results.
title: Late-Aligned Tail Recurrence With Learned Sublayer Scaling
